about: Known weak points for common BMW engines in US cars. First pass for the Walkaround listing checker.

how_to_read.shop_cost_usd: [low, high] in US dollars as stated by the source, or null when the source gave no figure. Never invented.
how_to_read.severity: Our own judgment of how bad it is if ignored: low, medium, high, critical.
how_to_read.risk: Our own overall rating for a used buyer.
how_to_read.us_models: Listed from general knowledge, not from the cited source. Verify before launch.
how_to_read.due_from_miles: Lowest mileage at which the source says the problem typically appears, as a number. Null when the source gave no mileage, meaning it can happen at any point.
how_to_read.liters: Engine size in liters and cylinder count, used to match the engine to the size a VIN decodes to.
how_to_read.also_codes: Closely related engine codes (usually low-emissions versions sold in some US states) treated as the same engine.
how_to_read.count_by_default: false when a problem is cosmetic or optional, so it is listed but not taken off the offer unless the buyer ticks it.

known_gaps: Many cost fields are empty and need real shop quotes
Each engine rests on one enthusiast source, a second source per engine is needed
The us_models lists here are general knowledge. The model-to-engine table the checker uses (data/models.json) was cross-checked on 2026-11-20, see its checked note
No per-model recall data yet, that comes from NHTSA by VIN

engines.verdict: The dependable choice. Known leaks and cooling parts, few expensive surprises.

problems.name: Electric water pump
problems.what_happens: Plastic pump fails and the engine overheats, sometimes at idle.

problems.name: Oil filter housing gasket
problems.what_happens: Oil leaks onto the drive belt. A soaked belt can slip or shred and damage the engine.
problems.note: Source calls this the most serious oil leak on the engine.

problems.name: Valve cover and gasket
problems.what_happens: Gasket hardens or the plastic cover cracks. Oil on plugs, burning oil smell.
problems.note: Source gives parts about $450 and 6 to 8 hours labor, no shop total.

problems.name: VANOS solenoids
problems.what_happens: Power loss, rough idle, limp mode.

problems.name: Lifter tick
problems.what_happens: Ticking when cold. Annoying, not harmful. Only engines built before December 2008.
problems.note: Permanent fix is a revised cylinder head, $3k+. Most owners live with it.

problems.name: Thermostat
problems.what_happens: Fails open (slow warm-up) or closed (overheating). Often done with the water pump.

engines.verdict: Fast and loved by tuners, but the most repair-prone six here. Buy only with records.

problems.name: Turbo wastegate rattle and turbo failure
problems.what_happens: Rattle, low boost codes, power loss, smoke.
problems.note: $3,500 independent, $6,000 dealer per source. Extended turbo warranty (10 yr / 82k) has long expired.

problems.name: High pressure fuel pump
problems.what_happens: Long crank, limp mode. Fails at random.
problems.note: Part about $450 plus install. Extended warranty (10 yr / 120k) has expired on age.

problems.name: Fuel injectors
problems.what_happens: Hard cold starts, misfires, rough idle.
problems.note: About $1,400 in parts for a set plus coding and labor.

problems.name: Electric water pump
problems.what_happens: Overheating, rapid coolant loss.

problems.name: Valve cover and gasket
problems.what_happens: Oil on plugs and coils, burning oil smell.
problems.note: Dealer labor alone about $1,000 per source.

problems.name: Carbon build-up on intake valves
problems.what_happens: Sluggish, misfires, hard starts. Needs walnut blasting.

problems.name: Plastic charge pipe
problems.what_happens: Cracks under boost, mostly on tuned cars.
problems.note: Upgraded pipe about $250 in parts.

engines.verdict: Fairly reliable, with a predictable list of gasket and cooling repairs around 80,000 to 100,000 miles.

problems.name: Valve cover and gasket
problems.what_happens: Oil on plugs, burning oil smell. The PCV valve is built into the cover and fails with it.
problems.note: $1,000 independent, $1,300 dealer per source.

problems.name: Electric water pump and thermostat
problems.what_happens: Sudden overheating with little warning.
problems.typical_miles: about 100,000 on average, some as early as 30,000 to 40,000

problems.name: Oil filter housing gasket
problems.what_happens: Oil drips onto the belt tensioner and drive belt.
problems.note: Replace the whole housing on cars past 100,000 miles.

problems.name: VANOS solenoids
problems.what_happens: Power loss, hesitation, rough idle.
problems.note: Two solenoids at about $165 each plus about $200 labor.

problems.name: High pressure fuel pump
problems.what_happens: Mostly 2010 and early to mid 2011 cars. No extended warranty on this engine.

also_reported: Plastic charge pipe cracking under boost

engines.desc: 2.0L four-cylinder turbo (N26 is the low-emissions version)
engines.risk: high for early builds, medium for later ones
engines.verdict: Build date decides everything. Early engines can destroy themselves when the timing chain guides break.

problems.name: Timing chain and oil pump chain guides
problems.what_happens: Plastic guides break up, the chain skips, and the engine can be destroyed with little warning. Often starts as a whine from the front of the engine.
problems.note: Class action covered 2012-2015 model years. BMW extended chain coverage to 7 yr / 70k, with partial help to 8 yr / 100k. That coverage has expired on age for these cars, so ask for proof the chain was replaced. Cost range is the settlement's caps: $3,000 for the chain job, $7,500 for a failed engine.

needs_checking: Exact build month when the revised chain guides went in (commonly cited as early 2015)

engines.desc: 2.0L four-cylinder turbo (B46 is the low-emissions version)
engines.verdict: A big step up from the N20. Very few common problems so far.

problems.name: Plastic oil filter housing
problems.what_happens: Housing cracks and can dump coolant within minutes, causing overheating.

problems.name: Valve cover gasket
problems.what_happens: Oil leak from the top of the engine.
problems.note: Pricey because injectors must come out.

problems.name: Cylinder head coolant vent line
problems.what_happens: Plastic line breaks and loses coolant fast.
problems.note: BMW fixes this free as a service action. Ask a dealer to check the VIN.

engines.verdict: Widely regarded as one of the most reliable engines BMW has made. The safest turbo six to buy used.

problems.name: Coolant loss
problems.what_happens: Low coolant warnings, often from the water pump or a leaky cap. Small top-ups can be normal.

problems.name: Valve cover gasket and PCV
problems.what_happens: Burning oil smell, oil on plugs. PCV diaphragm is built into the cover.

problems.name: VANOS solenoids
problems.what_happens: Hesitation, rough idle, limp mode.

problems.name: Oil filter breaking apart
problems.what_happens: Filter element shears and leaves a piece in the housing. Usually not serious.

engines.verdict: Cheap to buy, expensive to keep. Three known leaks that each cost four figures at a shop.

problems.name: Valve stem seals
problems.what_happens: Blue-white smoke on cold start or after idling, heavy oil use.
problems.note: Independent shop with the special tool. Used to be $5,000 to $10,000.

problems.name: Coolant transfer pipe
problems.what_happens: Coolant leaks from a pipe buried in the engine valley.
problems.note: $4,000+ if done the factory way.

problems.name: Alternator bracket gasket
problems.what_happens: Oil leak at the front of the engine.

problems.name: Valve cover gaskets
problems.what_happens: Oil leak and burning oil smell.

engines.verdict: The cheap V8 BMW is cheap for a reason. Avoid 2008-2013 engines unless the price leaves room for an engine.

problems.name: Oil consumption and valve stem seals
problems.what_happens: Burns a quart every 600 to 1,000 miles, white smoke from the tailpipes.
problems.note: Seal job requires dropping the engine.

problems.name: Timing chain stretch
problems.what_happens: 2008-2014 engines. Chain can jump and bend valves.
problems.note: Can exceed $15,000 per source.

problems.name: Fuel injectors
problems.what_happens: Rough idle, misfires, black soot on the bumper.
problems.note: $200 to $300 per injector, eight of them, plus labor.

problems.name: Battery drain
problems.what_happens: Batteries wear out fast. BMW calls for a new one every other oil change.

engines.buyer_note: Ask whether BMW's Customer Care Package work (2014-2015) was done and get it in writing from a dealer by VIN. Source advises 2016 or newer.

engines.verdict: A special engine with one big question: have the rod bearings been replaced, and when.

problems.name: Rod bearing wear
problems.what_happens: Bearings wear early. If one fails, the engine is destroyed. Preventive replacement is the norm.
problems.note: Source recommends preventive replacement at 40,000 to 50,000 miles. Cost not in source, needs a shop quote.

problems.name: Throttle actuators
problems.what_happens: Check engine light, limp mode. Two actuators, labor heavy.

problems.name: VANOS solenoids and seals
problems.what_happens: Rough idle, lost low-end torque.

problems.name: Oil consumption
problems.what_happens: Uses oil between changes.

engines.desc: 3.0L inline-six, twin turbo (M2 Competition, M3, M4)
engines.verdict: Solid for an M engine. The famous crank hub issue is rare on stock cars.

problems.name: Crank hub slip
problems.what_happens: Sudden limp mode and rough running when the timing slips. Source puts reports under 1% of cars.
problems.note: More of a concern on tuned cars. Ask if the car has been tuned.

problems.name: Valve cover and gasket
problems.what_happens: Burning oil smell, oil on plugs.

problems.name: Oil pan gasket
problems.what_happens: Slow leak. Subframe has to come down.
problems.note: One reader reported a $4,500 dealer quote.

problems.name: Oil filter housing gasket
problems.what_happens: Oil leak onto the belt.
